metadata.title: The Crossing Tverberg Theorem
metadata.authors: Radoslav Fulek, Bernd Gartner, Andrey Kupavskii, Pavel Valtr, Uli Wagner

nodes.name: General position
nodes.statement: A set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in \emph{general position} if no $d+1$ points are on a common hyperplane (e.g., no three points on a line in the plane).

nodes.name: Crossing convex polytopes
nodes.statement: Two convex polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ \emph{cross} if their boundaries have a non-empty intersection. (A non-full-dimensional polytope coincides with its boundary.)

nodes.name: Crossing family
nodes.statement: A collection of disjoint segments that pairwise cross, i.e., their connecting segments pairwise intersect.

nodes.name: Tverberg point and Tverberg partition
nodes.statement: Given a partition of $X$ into $r$ sets whose convex hulls share a common point $o$: $o$ is a \emph{Tverberg point} and the partition is a \emph{Tverberg partition}.

nodes.name: Crossing Tverberg partition
nodes.statement: A Tverberg partition $X = X_1 \cup \cdots \cup X_r$ such that for any $X_i, X_j$ of size $d+1$, $\conv(X_i)$ and $\conv(X_j)$ cross.

nodes.name: Cocycle
nodes.statement: Given $n \geq k \geq 1$ and $|V|=n$, a family $\mathcal{C} \subset \binom{V}{k}$ is a \emph{cocycle} if $|\{F \in \mathcal{C}: F \subset M\}|$ is even for every $M \subset V$ with $|M|=k+1$.

nodes.name: Coboundary and elementary cocycle
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{D} \subset \binom{V}{k-1}$, the \emph{coboundary} is $\delta\mathcal{D} = \{F \in \binom{V}{k}: F \text{ contains an odd number of sets } D \in \mathcal{D}\}$. For a single $D$, $\delta D = \{F \in \binom{V}{k}: D \subset F\}$ is the \emph{elementary cocycle}.

nodes.name: Arrangement of pseudolines and pseudolinear drawing
nodes.statement: An \emph{arrangement of pseudolines} is a finite set of non-self-intersecting open arcs in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that any two cross transversely once and each disconnects the plane. A drawing of $K_n$ is \emph{pseudolinear} if its edges extend to such an arrangement.

nodes.name: Simple drawing of a graph
nodes.statement: A drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges intersects at most once, either at a common end point or in a proper crossing.

nodes.name: Tverberg's theorem
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a set of at least $(d+1)(r-1)+1$ points in $d$-space. Then $X$ can be partitioned into $r$ sets whose convex hulls all have a point $o$ in common.
conclusions: There is a partition $X = X_1 \cup \cdots \cup X_r$ with $\bigcap_{i=1}^r \conv(X_i) \neq \emptyset$

nodes.name: Tverberg theorem with bounded part sizes
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a set of at least $(d+1)(r-1)+1$ and at most $(d+1)r$ points in $d$-space. Then $X$ can be partitioned into $r$ disjoint sets $X_1, \ldots, X_r$ of size at most $d+1$ whose convex hulls all share a point.
conclusions: There is a partition into $r$ sets each of size $\leq d+1$
$\bigcap_{i=1}^r \conv(X_i) \neq \emptyset$

nodes.name: Crossing Tverberg theorem (bounded case)
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a set of at least $(d+1)(r-1)+1$ and at most $(d+1)r$ points in $d$-space. Then $X$ can be partitioned into $r$ disjoint sets $X_1, \ldots, X_r$ of size at most $d+1$, whose convex hulls share a point and such that for any $X_i, X_j$ of size $d+1$, $\conv(X_i)$ and $\conv(X_j)$ cross.
conclusions: There is a Tverberg partition into $r$ sets of size $\leq d+1$
Any two parts of size $d+1$ have crossing convex hulls

nodes.name: Crossing Tverberg partition for $|X|=(d+1)r$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a set of $(d+1)r$ points in $d$-space. Then $X$ partitions into $r$ sets $X_1, \ldots, X_r$ of size $d+1$ whose convex hulls share a point and pairwise cross.
conclusions: Partition into $r$ sets of size exactly $d+1$
Their convex hulls share a common point
All pairs of convex hulls cross

nodes.name: Pairwise crossing simplices on $n$ points
nodes.statement: For every finite point set $X$ of size $n$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ in general position, there exist $\lfloor n/(d+1) \rfloor$ vertex-disjoint and pairwise crossing simplices with vertices in $X$. In particular, in the plane there are $\lfloor n/3 \rfloor$ pairwise crossing triangles.
conclusions: $\lfloor n/(d+1) \rfloor$ vertex-disjoint pairwise crossing simplices exist with vertices in $X$

nodes.name: Crossing Tverberg theorem
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a set of at least $(d+1)(r-1)+1$ points in $d$-space. Then $X$ can be partitioned into $r$ sets whose convex hulls share a common point, and for any $X_i, X_j$ of size at least $d+1$, $\conv(X_i)$ and $\conv(X_j)$ cross.
conclusions: $X$ admits a Tverberg partition into $r$ sets
Any two parts of size $\geq d+1$ have crossing convex hulls

nodes.name: Unnesting lemma
nodes.statement: Let $T, T'$ be two disjoint $(d+1)$-element sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\nula \in \conv(T) \cap \conv(T')$. Then there exist disjoint $(d+1)$-element sets $S, S'$ with $S \cup S' = T \cup T'$, $\nula \in \conv(S) \cap \conv(S')$, and $\conv(S), \conv(S')$ cross.
conclusions: There exist disjoint $S, S'$ with $S \cup S' = T \cup T'$, $|S|=|S'|=d+1$
$\nula \in \conv(S) \cap \conv(S')$
$\conv(S)$ and $\conv(S')$ cross

nodes.name: Stronger Crossing Tverberg theorem (size-preserving)
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a set of points in $d$-space and suppose there is a Tverberg partition into $r$ parts of sizes $s_1, \ldots, s_r$ with $s_i \leq d+1$ and Tverberg point $o$. Then there is also a \emph{crossing} Tverberg partition into $r$ parts of the same sizes with Tverberg point $o$.
assumptions: There is a Tverberg partition with parts of sizes $s_1, \ldots, s_r$, all $\leq d+1$
$o$ is a Tverberg point of this partition
conclusions: There exists a crossing Tverberg partition into parts of the same sizes
$o$ is still a Tverberg point of the new partition

nodes.name: Parity lemma
nodes.statement: Let $V \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|V|=2(d+1)$ such that $V \cup \{\nula\}$ is in general position. Then $|\{\{F,G\}: F,G \in \binom{V}{d+1}, F \cap G = \emptyset, \nula \in \conv F \cap \conv G\}|$ is even.
conclusions: The number of partitions $\{F,G\}$ of $V$ into equal halves with $\nula \in \conv F \cap \conv G$ is even

nodes.name: Origin-containing $(d+1)$-subsets form a cocycle
nodes.statement: Let $V \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $V \cup \{\nula\}$ in general position. Then $\mathcal{C}(V) := \{F \in \binom{V}{d+1}: \nula \in \conv F\}$ is a cocycle.
conclusions: $\mathcal{C}(V) = \{F \in \binom{V}{d+1}: \nula \in \conv F\}$ is a cocycle

nodes.name: Disjoint pairs in any cocycle are even-counted
nodes.statement: Let $k \geq 1$, $|V|=2k$, and $\mathcal{C} \subset \binom{V}{k}$ be a cocycle. Set $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}} := \{\{F,G\}: F, G \in \mathcal{C}, F \cap G = \emptyset\}$. Then $|\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}|$ is even.
conclusions: $|\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}|$ is even, where $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}$ is the set of disjoint pairs $\{F,G\}$ in $\mathcal{C}$

nodes.name: Every cocycle is a coboundary
nodes.statement: For every cocycle $\mathcal{C} \subset \binom{V}{k}$ there exists a family $\mathcal{D} \subset \binom{V}{k-1}$ such that $\mathcal{C} = \delta\mathcal{D} = \delta D_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus \delta D_m$, where $\oplus$ is symmetric difference.
conclusions: There is $\mathcal{D} \subset \binom{V}{k-1}$ with $\mathcal{C} = \delta\mathcal{D}$

nodes.name: Symmetric difference of cocycle pairs
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C} \oplus \delta D} = \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}} \oplus \mathcal{R}$, where $\mathcal{R} := \{\{F, G\}: F \in \delta D, G \in \mathcal{C}, F \cap G = \emptyset\}$.
conclusions: $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C} \oplus \delta D} = \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}} \oplus \mathcal{R}$

nodes.name: Topological Tverberg theorem
nodes.statement: If $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $r$ is a prime power, then for every continuous map from the $(d+1)(r-1)$-dimensional simplex $\Delta_{(d+1)(r-1)}$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, there exist $r$ pairwise disjoint faces of $\Delta_{(d+1)(r-1)}$ whose images intersect in a common point.
conclusions: There exist $r$ pairwise disjoint faces of $\Delta_{(d+1)(r-1)}$ whose $\mu$-images intersect

nodes.name: Crossing triangles in pseudolinear drawings of $K_{3n}$
nodes.statement: In a pseudolinear drawing of a complete graph $K_{3n}$ we can find $m=(1-o(1))n$ vertex-disjoint and pairwise crossing triangles, and the topological discs they bound share a common point.
conclusions: There exist $m = (1 - o(1)) n$ vertex-disjoint pairwise crossing triangles
Their bounded topological discs share a common point

nodes.name: Carath\'eodory's theorem
nodes.statement: If $x \in \conv(S) \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, then $x$ lies in the convex hull of at most $d+1$ points of $S$.
conclusions: There is $S' \subset S$ with $|S'| \leq d+1$ and $x \in \conv(S')$

nodes.name: Carath\'eodory's theorem for drawings of complete graphs
nodes.statement: An analog of Carath\'eodory's theorem holds in the setting of drawings of complete graphs (used to extract a small set of triangle-images covering a common point).
assumptions: Drawing of a complete graph in the plane
conclusions: Common-point extraction analogous to Carath\'eodory's theorem

nodes.name: Pach-Solymosi-Toth canonical-subdrawing theorem
nodes.statement: Every simple drawing of $K_n$ contains a drawing of $K_m$ that is weakly isomorphic to a convex complete graph or a twisted complete graph, with $m \geq \Omega(\log^{1/6} n)$.
conclusions: There is $K_m \subset K_n$ weakly isomorphic to a convex or twisted $K_m$, $m \geq \Omega(\log^{1/6} n)$

nodes.name: Fox-Pach pairwise crossing edges in $K_n$
nodes.statement: Every simple drawing of $K_n$ contains $\Omega(n^\varepsilon)$ pairwise crossing edges, for some $\varepsilon > 0$.
conclusions: There exist $\Omega(n^\varepsilon)$ pairwise crossing edges in $\mathcal{D}$

nodes.name: Mulzer-Werner approximate Tverberg
nodes.statement: An approximate Tverberg partition of size $\lceil |X|/(4(d+1)^3) \rceil$ can be computed in time $d^{O(\log d)|X|}$.
conclusions: An approximate Tverberg partition of size $\lceil |X|/(4(d+1)^3) \rceil$ is computable in $d^{O(\log d)|X|}$ time

nodes.name: Teng's NP-completeness for Tverberg-point verification
nodes.statement: Checking whether a given point is a Tverberg point of a given point set is NP-complete.
assumptions: Input: a finite point set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and a query point $q$
conclusions: Deciding whether $q$ is a Tverberg point of $X$ is NP-complete

nodes.name: $\delta D$ is an elementary cocycle
nodes.statement: For $D \in \binom{V}{k-1}$, the family $\delta D = \{F \in \binom{V}{k}: D \subset F\}$ is a cocycle: for any $M$ with $|M|=k+1$, $|\{F \in \delta D: F \subset M\}| \in \{0, 2\}$.
conclusions: $\delta D$ is a cocycle

nodes.name: $K_4$ in a pseudolinear drawing
nodes.statement: Every four vertices in a pseudolinear drawing of a complete graph induce either a crossing-free $K_4$ or a $K_4$ with exactly one pair of crossing edges in the interior of a disc bounded by a crossing-free 4-cycle.
assumptions: Pseudolinear drawing of a complete graph
conclusions: The induced sub-drawing of $K_4$ is one of two specific configurations

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem on bounded-size Tverberg partition (TP420.2)
nodes.statement: Apply Tverberg's theorem to obtain $X'_1, \ldots, X'_r$ with common point $o = $ origin. By Carath\'eodory's theorem, from each $X'_i$ of size $> d+1$ pick $d+1$ points whose convex hull still contains the origin; redistribute the removed points to fill smaller $X'_i$'s up to size $d+1$. The origin remains a common point.

nodes.name: Proof of Crossing Tverberg theorem (TP420.4) from TP420.3 and CP420.1
nodes.statement: If $|X| \leq (d+1)r$ apply Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. Otherwise apply CP420.1 to a subset $Y \subset X$ of size $(d+1)r$, then add remaining points one by one to inclusion-minimal sets, preserving crossings.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} (TP420.3) via Fixing Pairs
nodes.statement: Start from a Tverberg partition with parts of size $\leq d+1$ (TP420.2). While there is a pair of nested simplices, repartition the $2(d+1)$ involved points using Lemma~\ref{lem:unnesting}; lex-decrease in volume sequence guarantees termination.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:unnesting} (LP420.1)
nodes.statement: Reduce to general-position $T \cup T' \cup \{\nula\}$ via perturbation; apply Parity Lemma (LP420.2) with $V = T \cup T'$ to get a second pair $\{S, S'\}$. At most one such pair is nested (the outer simplex is uniquely $\conv(T \cup T')$), so the other pair crosses.

nodes.name: Geometric proof of Parity Lemma (LP420.2) for $d=2$
nodes.statement: Place $V$ on a circle around origin; reflect each point. By circular structure, two consecutive points $p, p'$ have the same color (both in $V$). They are combinatorially indistinguishable: swapping them in any good split yields another good split, so the count is even.

nodes.name: Combinatorial proof of Parity Lemma (LP420.2)
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem1} (LP420.3), $\mathcal{C}(V)$ is a cocycle, and the result follows from Theorem~\ref{prop2} (TP420.6) on cocycles of $|V|=2k$ subsets.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem1} (LP420.3)
nodes.statement: Lift any $M = \{v_1, \ldots, v_{d+2}\}$ to dimension $d+1$ so the lifted set spans a full-dimensional simplex $\Delta$. The vertical line through $\nula$ meets $\partial\Delta$ in either 0 or 2 facet interiors, giving $|\{F \in \mathcal{C}(V): F \subset M\}| \in \{0,2\}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{prop2} (TP420.6)
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem2} (LP420.4), every cocycle is a sum of elementary cocycles $\delta D$. Show parity is preserved under symmetric difference with $\delta D$ via a counting argument on $\mathcal{R}$, using the cocycle property of $\mathcal{C}$ on $V \setminus D$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem2} (LP420.4)
nodes.statement: Pick $v \in V$. Define $\mathcal{D}_v := \{D \in \binom{V \setminus v}{k-1}: D \cup \{v\} \in \mathcal{C}\}$. Case analysis on whether $v \in F$ shows $\mathcal{C} = \delta \mathcal{D}_v$, using the cocycle property when $v \notin F$.

nodes.name: Proof of crossing triangles in pseudolinear drawings (TP420.8)
nodes.statement: Apply Topological Tverberg with $r=m$ (largest prime power $\leq n$) to a continuous extension $\mu: \Delta_{3m-3} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ of the drawing. Apply analog of Lemma~\ref{lem1} for fixing operations; termination via volume-decrease using pseudolinear $K_4$ structure.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim ClP420.1
nodes.statement:
For pairs $\{F, G\}$ with $D 
ot\subset F$ and $D 
ot\subset G$ membership in both $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}$ and $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C} \oplus \delta D}$ agree. WLOG $D \subset F$ and $G \subset V \setminus D$: then $F \in \delta D$, so $F \in \mathcal{C}$ iff $F 
otin \mathcal{C} \oplus \delta D$, giving the claimed identity.

nodes.name: Fixing Pairs
nodes.statement: Iteratively repartition pairs of nested $(d+1)$-element parts in a Tverberg partition using Lemma~\ref{lem:unnesting} until no pair of nested simplices remains.
input: Tverberg partition $X_1, \ldots, X_r$ with parts of size $\leq d+1$ and common point $o$
output: Crossing Tverberg partition of $X$ into $r$ parts of the same sizes with the same Tverberg point $o$

nodes.name: Tverberg partition for $d=2, r=3$
nodes.statement: 9 points in the plane illustrate two distinct Tverberg partitions into 3 sets whose convex hulls share a common point, demonstrating possible nested-triangle configurations.

nodes.name: Fixing a pair of nested simplices
nodes.statement: 6 points form two nested triangles (red); after one fixing operation, the same 6 points form two crossing triangles (blue), illustrating Lemma~\ref{lem:unnesting}.

nodes.name: 8-point counterexample for linked tetrahedra in $\mathbb{R}^3$
nodes.statement: The 8 points $(3,-2,2), (2,-5,3), (-3,0,-4), (-1,2,0), (1,-5,-4), (4,1,-2), (-2,-5,-4), (-3,1,3)$ admit a pair of disjoint origin-containing tetrahedra but no two disjoint tetrahedra both containing the origin with a pair of linked 2-faces.

nodes.name: Crossing Tverberg partition in twisted $K_{3n}$
nodes.statement: For a twisted drawing of $K_{3n}$ with vertices labeled $0, \ldots, 3n-1$, the partition $\{\{i, n+i, 2n+i\}: i=0,\ldots,n-1\}$ is a crossing Tverberg partition.

nodes.name: Elementary cocycle $\delta D$
nodes.statement: For fixed $D \in \binom{V}{k-1}$, $\delta D = \{F \in \binom{V}{k}: D \subset F\}$ is a cocycle: a $(k+1)$-set $M$ either avoids $D$ (zero subsets in $\delta D$) or has $D = M \setminus \{p,q\}$ (exactly two).

nodes.name: Alternative termination measure (point count)
nodes.statement: Instead of volume, the number of points from $X$ inside $\conv(X_j)$ may be used as a lex-decreasing measure for the Fixing Pairs procedure.

nodes.name: Unusual parity-then-existence pattern
nodes.statement: Typically one proves an odd parity to ensure existence of one object. Here, evenness is exploited: given one nested pair, evenness of the parity count forces a second pair to exist, which must be crossing.

nodes.name: Aronov-Erdos-Goddard crossing-family conjecture
nodes.statement: Is there an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that every set of $n$ points in general position in the plane admits at least $cn$ disjoint pairs whose connecting segments pairwise cross?

nodes.name: Polynomial-iteration Fixing Pairs
nodes.statement: Prove or disprove that there is always a way to invoke the \emph{Fixing Pairs} operation only polynomially (or at least subexponentially) many times to reach a partition required by Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

nodes.name: Polynomial Tverberg partition
nodes.statement: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for finding a Tverberg partition (and a Tverberg point) of a given point set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$? Hardness within TFNP subclasses (PPAD, PLS, PPAD$\cap$PLS) is open.

nodes.name: Crossing Tverberg partition problem
nodes.statement: Given a finite set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|X| \geq (d+1)(r-1)+1$, find a partition $X = X_1 \cup \cdots \cup X_r$ that is a crossing Tverberg partition (Tverberg + pairwise crossing convex hulls of full-dimensional parts).

nodes.name: Apply Tverberg's theorem
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:Tverberg} to $X$, obtaining sets $X'_1, \ldots, X'_r$ whose convex hulls contain a common point, taken WLOG to be the origin.

nodes.name: Trim oversized parts via Carath\'eodory
nodes.statement: From every $X'_i$ of size $> d+1$, use Carath\'eodory's theorem to select $d+1$ points $X_i \subseteq X'_i$ whose convex hull still contains the origin.

nodes.name: Fill undersized parts
nodes.statement: Fill up parts $X'_i$ of size $< d+1$ with the points removed from other $X'_j$'s. The origin remains a common point of all $\conv(X_i)$.

nodes.name: Initial Tverberg partition
nodes.statement: Start with a Tverberg partition into sets of size $\leq d+1$ guaranteed by Theorem~\ref{thm:Tverberg2} (TP420.2).

nodes.name: Iteratively fix nested pairs
nodes.statement: While there is a pair of nested simplices $\conv(X_i) \subset \conv(X_j)$, apply the unnesting lemma (LP420.1) to repartition the $2(d+1)$ involved points into $S, S'$ that cross.

nodes.name: Volume sequence strictly decreases lexicographically
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{V} = (V_1, \ldots, V_s)$ be the volumes of full-dimensional simplices in decreasing order. After fixing $\conv(X_i) \subset \conv(X_j)$, the new simplices $\conv(S), \conv(S')$ are both volume-wise smaller than $\conv(X_j)$. Hence $\mathcal{V}'$ agrees with $\mathcal{V}$ in the first $k-1$ positions but $V'_k < V_k$.

nodes.name: Termination from total order
nodes.statement: Lex order on real-valued volume sequences is total, so the iteration terminates, leaving a crossing Tverberg partition.

nodes.name: Reduce to general position
nodes.statement: Reduce to the case where $T \cup T' \cup \{\nula\}$ is in general position via a small perturbation: general position is achieved generically, and the property of \emph{not} having sets $S, S'$ as required is preserved under small perturbations.

nodes.name: Apply Parity Lemma to $V = T \cup T'$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lemparity} (LP420.2): the number of partitions $\{F, G\}$ of $V$ into equal halves with $\nula \in \conv F \cap \conv G$ is even, hence at least 2 (since $\{T, T'\}$ is one).

nodes.name: Uniqueness of nested outer simplex
nodes.statement: At most one of the pairs $\{F, G\}$ can be nested: the outer simplex of a nested pair coincides with $\conv(T \cup T')$ and is uniquely determined.

nodes.name: Conclude crossing pair exists
nodes.statement: Hence at least one of the (at least two) pairs yields crossing simplices $\{S, S'\}$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Place points on circle
nodes.statement: Since the parity statement is invariant under positive scaling, assume all 6 points of $V$ lie on a circle centered at the origin. By general position, no two points are antipodal.

nodes.name: Reflect and find consecutive same-color pair
nodes.statement: Reflect each point through the origin (white). The 12 points cannot fully alternate around the circle, so two consecutive ones share a color; WLOG both are black, i.e., in $V$. Call them $p, p'$.

nodes.name: Combinatorial indistinguishability of $p, p'$
nodes.statement: Observation (i): $p$ and $p'$ cannot belong to the same triple $F \subset V$ with $\nula \in \conv(F)$. Observation (ii): for any third $q$, the segments $pq$ and $p'q$ have the origin on the same side.

nodes.name: Swapping induces matching
nodes.statement: In any counted partition $\{F, G\}$, $p$ and $p'$ lie in different parts and swapping them yields another counted partition. This pairing is a fixed-point-free involution, so the number of counted partitions is even.

nodes.name: Lift $M$ to a $(d+1)$-simplex
nodes.statement: For $M = \{v_1, \ldots, v_{d+2}\} \subset V$, lift the points to $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ so that the convex hull of the lifted set $\hat M$ is a full-dimensional simplex $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Vertical line meets $\partial\Delta$ in 0 or 2 facets
nodes.statement: Each $\hat F \subset \hat M$ of size $d+1$ spans a facet of $\Delta$, and $\nula \in \conv F$ iff the vertical line through $\nula$ meets that facet. By general position, this line meets $\partial \Delta$ in 0 or 2 points, each in some facet's interior.

nodes.name: Conclude cocycle property
nodes.statement: Therefore $|\{F \in \mathcal{C}(V): F \subset M\}| \in \{0, 2\}$ for every $(d+2)$-subset $M$, proving $\mathcal{C}(V)$ is a cocycle.

nodes.name: Reduce to invariance under $\oplus \delta D$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem2} (LP420.4), every cocycle $\mathcal{C}$ equals $\delta D_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus \delta D_m$. It suffices to show $|\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}| \equiv |\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C} \oplus \delta D}| \pmod 2$ for any $D$.

nodes.name: Identity $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C} \oplus \delta D} = \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}} \oplus \mathcal{R}$
nodes.statement: Establish via case split on whether $D$ is contained in $F$ or $G$ that $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C} \oplus \delta D} = \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}} \oplus \mathcal{R}$ where $\mathcal{R} = \{\{F, G\}: F \in \delta D, G \in \mathcal{C}, F \cap G = \emptyset\}$.

nodes.name: Even count of $\mathcal{R}$
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{C}$ is a cocycle and $|V \setminus D| = k+1$, there is an even number of $G \in \mathcal{C}$ with $G \subset V \setminus D$. Each such $G$ pairs uniquely with $F = V \setminus G \in \delta D$, so $|\mathcal{R}|$ is even.

nodes.name: Conclude parity preserved
nodes.statement: Combining steps gives $|\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C}}| \equiv |\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{C} \oplus \delta D}| \pmod 2$, completing the proof of Theorem~\ref{prop2}.

nodes.name: Pick $v \in V$ and define $\mathcal{D}_v$
nodes.statement: Choose an arbitrary $v \in V$ and define $\mathcal{D}_v := \{D \in \binom{V \setminus v}{k-1}: D \cup \{v\} \in \mathcal{C}\}$.

nodes.name: Case $v \in F$
nodes.statement: If $v \in F$, then $F \setminus \{v\}$ is the unique element of $\binom{V \setminus v}{k-1}$ contained in $F$; thus $F \in \mathcal{C}$ iff $F \setminus \{v\} \in \mathcal{D}_v$ iff $F \in \delta\mathcal{D}_v$.

nodes.name: Case $v \notin F$
nodes.statement: If $v \notin F$, set $M = F \cup \{v\}$ with $|M| = k+1$. Cocycle property: $|\mathcal{C} \cap \binom{M}{k}|$ is even, so $F \in \mathcal{C}$ iff $M$ contains an odd number of $G \in \mathcal{C}$ with $v \in G$, iff $F$ contains an odd number of $D = G \setminus \{v\} \in \mathcal{D}_v$, iff $F \in \delta\mathcal{D}_v$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\mathcal{C} = \delta\mathcal{D}_v$
nodes.statement: Both cases give $F \in \mathcal{C} \Leftrightarrow F \in \delta\mathcal{D}_v$, hence $\mathcal{C} = \delta\mathcal{D}_v$.

nodes.name: Choose $m$ as largest prime power $\leq n$
nodes.statement: Set $m$ to be the largest prime power not larger than $n$; the asymptotic prime distribution gives $m = (1 - o(1)) n$.

nodes.name: Construct continuous extension $\mu$
nodes.statement: Define $\mu: \Delta_{3m-3} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ to extend $\mathcal{D}$ on the 1-skeleton (as drawing of some $K_{3m-2}$), then map each 2-face homeomorphically into the plane, extending continuously elsewhere.

nodes.name: Apply Topological Tverberg
nodes.statement: Apply the Topological Tverberg theorem (TP420.7) with $r = m$, $d = 2$, and Carath\'eodory for drawings (TP420.10) to get $m-1$ disjoint 2-faces $F_1, \ldots, F_{m-1}$ whose images share a point.

nodes.name: Topological fixing operations
nodes.statement: Use a topological version of Lemma~\ref{lem1} (LP420.3) to fix non-crossing pairs of $T_i = \partial F_i$ in $K_{3m-2}$.

nodes.name: Termination via pseudolinear $K_4$ structure
nodes.statement: By PrP420.2, every 4 vertices in a pseudolinear drawing form one of two specific $K_4$ patterns; this forces $\mu(uv)$ avoiding $T_j$, so a volume argument on $\mu(F_i)$ gives lex-decreasing volumes and termination.

nodes.name: Initialize Tverberg partition
nodes.statement: Compute a Tverberg partition $X_1, \ldots, X_r$ of $X$ with parts of size $\leq d+1$ and common point $o$ (e.g., via Theorem~\ref{thm:Tverberg2}).

nodes.name: Loop: while a nested pair exists
nodes.statement: While there is a pair $(X_i, X_j)$ of $(d+1)$-element parts with $\conv(X_i) \subset \conv(X_j)$, apply the unnesting lemma (LP420.1) to repartition the $2(d+1)$ points into $S, S'$ with $\nula \in \conv(S) \cap \conv(S')$ and $\conv(S), \conv(S')$ crossing, then replace $X_i, X_j$ with $S, S'$.

nodes.name: Return crossing partition
nodes.statement: When no nested pairs remain, return the current partition $X_1, \ldots, X_r$ as a crossing Tverberg partition.
